descriptions.description: Section 44A establishes a procedure for voluntary amalgamation of banking companies. A draft scheme containing the terms of amalgamation must be separately placed before each company’s shareholders and approved by a majority in number representing two-thirds in value of those present personally or by proxy. Meeting notice must be given to every shareholder and published weekly for three consecutive weeks in at least two qualifying newspapers. Dissenting shareholders may claim the Reserve Bank-determined value of their shares if the scheme is sanctioned. After the requisite shareholder approval, the scheme must be submitted to the Reserve Bank; sanction makes it binding. Upon sanction, property and liabilities transfer to the acquiring banking company subject to the sanctioned scheme, and the Reserve Bank may order dissolution of the amalgamated company.
evidence: no banking company shall be amalgamated with another banking company, unless a scheme containing the terms of such amalgamation has been placed in draft before the shareholders of each of the banking companies concerned separately

On the sanctioning of a scheme of amalgamation by the Reserve Bank, the properly of the amalgamated banking company shall, by virtue of the order of sanction, be transferred to and vest in, and the liabilities of the said company shall, by virtue of the said order be transferred to, and become the liabilities of, the banking company

descriptions.description: Section 45 creates an RBI/Central Government regime for moratorium, reconstruction, or amalgamation of a banking company. Where the Reserve Bank considers there is good reason, it may seek a Central Government moratorium, which may stay actions and proceedings for a total period not exceeding six months and generally restrict payments, liability discharges, loans, advances, and investments. During a moratorium or at any other time, the Reserve Bank may prepare a reconstruction or amalgamation scheme when satisfied that this is necessary in the public interest, depositors’ interests, proper management, or the banking system’s interests. The scheme may regulate assets, liabilities, creditors, members, employees, proceedings, and consequential matters. After consultation on a draft, Central Government sanction brings the scheme into force and makes it binding according to its terms.
evidence: if the Reserve Bank is satisfied that- (a) in the public interest; or (b) in the interests of the depositors; or (c) in order to secure the proper management of the banking company; or (d) in the interests of the banking system of the country as a whole, it is necessary so to do, the Reserve Bank may prepare a scheme

the properties and assets of the banking company shall, by virtue of and to the extent provided in the scheme, stand transferred to, and vest in, and the liabilities of the banking company shall, by virtue of and to the extent provided in the scheme, stand transferred to, and become the liabilities of the transferee bank
descriptions.limitations: This unit covers the section 45 RBI/Central Government moratorium and reconstruction/amalgamation mechanism, including its statutory conditions and override provisions. An individual scheme is still necessary to determine the particular transfers and terms. descriptions.description: Section 9 of the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1980 authorizes the Central Government, after consultation with the Reserve Bank, to make schemes carrying out the Act. Such a scheme may address the capital and board structure of a corresponding new bank and may provide for its reconstitution, amalgamation with another corresponding new bank or banking institution, or transfer of all or part of an undertaking between specified banking institutions. The Central Government may amend or vary a scheme after RBI consultation. When a scheme concerning those restructuring matters comes into operation, it binds the affected institutions, members, depositors, creditors, employees, and other persons with relevant rights or liabilities. Property, assets, and liabilities transfer and vest only by virtue of and to the extent provided in the scheme.

descriptions.description: The New Bank of India (Amalgamation and Transfer of Undertaking) Scheme, 1993 was made by the Central Government under section 9 of the 1980 Act after consultation with the Reserve Bank, and was appointed to commence on 4 September 1993. It defines Punjab National Bank as the transferee bank and New Bank of India as the transferor bank. On commencement, New Bank of India’s undertakings transfer to and vest in Punjab National Bank. The transferred undertaking encompasses assets, rights, property, records, borrowings, liabilities, and obligations. Leased property is treated as held by the transferee as lessee; existing contracts and instruments continue in its favour or against it; and pending proceedings may continue by or against it. The Scheme also dissolves the transferor’s board and provides for transferor-bank employees and employee funds.

descriptions.description: Section 16 regulates the lawfulness of sub-letting and later transfers of tenancy rights under the reproduced Delhi Rent Control Act provision. A pre-9 June 1952 sub-letting is deemed lawful, despite lack of landlord consent, when the sub-tenant remains in occupation at commencement of the Act. By contrast, premises sub-let on or after 9 June 1952 without the landlord’s written consent are not deemed lawfully sub-let. After commencement of the Act, a tenant may neither sub-let the whole or part of the premises nor transfer or assign tenancy rights, in whole or part, without the landlord’s previous written consent. The provision also bars a landlord from claiming or receiving any premium, pugree, or other cash or in-kind consideration for giving consent to sub-letting.
evidence: No premises which have been sub-let either in whole or in part on or after the 9th day of June, 1952, without obtaining the consent in writing of the landlord, shall be deemed to have been lawfully sub-let.

After the commencement of this Act, no tenant shall, without the previous consent in writing of the landlord, -(a) sub-let the whole or any part of the premises held by him as a tenant; or(b) transfer or assign his rights in the tenancy or in any part thereof.

descriptions.description: Section 17 provides notice procedures concerning sub-tenancies. Where, after commencement of the Act, premises are sub-let in whole or part with the landlord’s previous written consent, the tenant or sub-tenant may give prescribed notice to the landlord of the creation of the sub-tenancy within one month and may notify its termination within one month of termination. For premises lawfully sub-let before commencement, the tenant or sub-tenant may give prescribed notice of creation within six months of commencement and notice of termination within one month. If, in the latter category, the landlord disputes that the sub-letting was lawful, either the landlord or sub-tenant may apply to the Controller within two months of the relevant notice event, and the Controller must decide the dispute.

the Controller shall decide the dispute.

descriptions.description: Section 18 specifies circumstances in which a sub-tenant is deemed to become a direct tenant under the landlord. Under subsection (1), where an eviction order under section 14 is made against the tenant but not against a sub-tenant referred to in section 17, and notice of that sub-tenancy has been given to the landlord, the sub-tenant becomes, from the date of the eviction order, a tenant directly under the landlord for the occupied premises on the same terms and conditions the original tenant would have had if the tenancy continued. Under subsection (2), where before commencement of the Act a tenant’s interest was determined without determining a lawful sub-tenant’s interest, that sub-tenant becomes a direct tenant from commencement of the Act on corresponding terms and conditions.
evidence: the sub-tenant shall, with effect from the date of the order, be deemed to become a tenant holding directly under the landlord
the sub-tenant shall, with effect from the date of the commencement of this Act, be deemed to have become a tenant holding directly under the landlord
